synthesis: The source turns local pole behavior into a global quadratic height in two stages: valuation lemmas translate the elliptic group law into placewise identities, and the residue-degree-weighted product formula cancels the remaining coordinate-difference terms to prove the parallelogram law for d. Since d is visibly nonnegative on integer combinations, Lemma 3 then forces every associated binary height form to have nonpositive discriminant.
source_support: Units d02 and d04 define the weighted valuation setting and d; d05-d08 derive the local addition and valuation relations, with the constant nonzero discriminant excluding simultaneous positive valuations; d09 explicitly applies those lemmas and the product formula to obtain d(P-Q)+d(P+Q)=2d(P)+2d(Q); and d10 uses d(mP+nQ)>=0 with Lemma 3 to deduce the discriminant inequality.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes a local-to-global mechanism with a second positivity-to-discriminant mechanism: local group-law valuation identities are globally summed by the product formula to create the quadratic law, after which lattice nonnegativity constrains its real discriminant.
limits: The result is established for the displayed elliptic curve over the constant-defined function field K/k. Several group-law, product-formula, and summed-identity displays are OCR-damaged, so formula-level reuse requires scan verification; these units do not establish the paper's announced broader generalization.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct parent units supply indispensable successive links rather than parallel paraphrases: the valuation framework, local lemmas, global product-formula cancellation, and the lattice argument jointly establish the claimed positive-semidefinite quadratic structure.

synthesis: Applying the positive-semidefinite height to the generic point P0 and its Frobenius image Q0 identifies the diagonal coefficients as 1 and q. The finite splitting cases, together with the infinite-place contribution, identify the mixed coefficient as q-N; substituting these three values into the nonpositive-discriminant inequality converts height positivity into the stated point-count bound.
source_support: Unit d10 proves the height discriminant is nonpositive. Unit d11 states that Lemma 4's values d(P0)=1, d(Q0)=q, and d(P0+Q0)-d(P0)-d(Q0)=q-N make that inequality equivalent to the theorem. Unit d12 computes the two diagonal heights from the unique ramified infinite place, while d13-d15 classify the finite primes detected by x-x^q and their point-count and pole contributions. Unit d16 combines N=2L+M, the finite contributions, and the infinite-place valuation to obtain the mixed coefficient q-N.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis substitutes arithmetic-geometric data into an abstract quadratic-form constraint: Frobenius scales one diagonal height, prime splitting translates rational-point incidence into pole weights, and their aggregate becomes the cross term whose discriminant bounds N.
limits: This calculation is specific to the given elliptic function field, Frobenius pair, and degree-two splitting analysis. The OCR severely damages the intermediate total for d(P0+Q0), so its term-by-term layout must be scan-checked even though the surrounding counts and final mixed-term identity are explicit.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parents jointly support a complete dependency unavailable from any one unit: general height positivity, the Frobenius specialization, diagonal-height computation, local splitting contributions, and final accounting are all explicitly connected by the source.

synthesis: For primes detected by x-x^q, the quadratic extension separates three behaviors: ramified degree-one places represent k-points and contribute poles, split degree-one places represent k-points but contribute no pole, and inert degree-two places represent no k-point but do contribute poles. Thus residue-field rationality and group-law height contribution are distinct filters, and their mismatch drives the later identity between N and the mixed height term.
source_support: Unit d13 connects k-solutions with degree-one primes and shows that finite poles of x(P0+Q0) can occur only at primes dividing x-x^q. Unit d14 treats ramified degree-one primes, obtaining pole valuation -2 and the count M. Unit d15 contrasts split degree-one primes, counted by 2L solutions with nonnegative x-valuation, against inert degree-two primes, counted by q-L-M with valuation -2 and no k-solution. Unit d16 records N=2L+M and aggregates these contributions into q-N.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis cross-classifies the same primes by two non-equivalent outputs—whether their residue coordinates are k-rational and whether elliptic addition produces a pole—revealing why point counting and height accounting use different weights before recombining.
limits: The trichotomy and counts apply to primes above factors of x^q-x in the chosen quadratic extension K/k(x), not to arbitrary splitting situations. Factorization and coordinate identities are OCR-damaged, so exact algebraic displays require scan verification, although the cases, valuations, and counts are readable.
quality_reason: Accepted because d13-d16 explicitly support a concrete contrast across distinct units: the detection criterion, ramified contribution, split/inert mismatch, and terminal accounting together yield more than a shared theme or paraphrase.
